=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:63 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The shipped-workflow exclusion uses exact-path array membership via contains(fromJson('[...bare paths...]'), github.event.workflow_run.path), but workflow_run.path includes a ref suffix (e.g., .github/workflows/ai-review.yml@refs/heads/main). contains() for arrays checks exact element equality, so the ref-suffixed runtime path never matches any bare-path entry in the exclusion array.
  WHY: A failed pull-request run of a shipped consumer workflow (AI Review, AI Implement, etc.) bypasses the exclusion. The triage-workflow-run job dispatches the reusable triage workflow, which opens an unintended ai:check-triage issue and enters the normal clarify-to-review pipeline. Existing tests in test_review_merge_train.py:714-720 confirm the ref-suffixed path format. The triage trigger test in test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:64-77 uses bare paths without ref suffixes and does not cover this runtime path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

If `workflow_run.path` includes ref suffixes in some contexts (as indicated by the consensus reviewer findings), this exclusion logic will fail, potentially causing the triage workflow to triage itself and creating an infinite loop.
  WHY: The triage workflow could trigger on its own workflow runs if the path does not match the exact string in the exclusion list, leading to duplicate triage issues and recursive pipeline activity.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml: line 63 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The exclusion list compares the `workflow_run.path` value against unsuffixed wrapper paths (e.g. `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`), but real `workflow_run.path` values include a `@refs/heads/<branch>` suffix. The existing repository already documents this shape in `tests/test_review_merge_train.py:719` (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml@refs/heads/main`), `tests/test_review_merge_train.py:738` (`acme/consumer/.github/workflows/internal-review.yml@refs/heads/main`), `tests/test_review_merge_train.py:752` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/main`), and `tests/test_review_merge_train.py:877` (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml@refs/heads main`). None of those strings match the literal entries in the exclusion array, so a failed pull-request run of a shipped consumer wrapper (e.g. `AI Review`, `AI Plan`, `AI Clarify`) is not excluded and proceeds to dispatch the reusable triage workflow, which opens an unintended `ai:check-triage` issue for it. The companion test at `tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:64` constructs the event with `path = ".github/workflows/test.yml"` (no suffix) and `tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:136` asserts `_run_event("Any name", path=own)` against the same unsuffixed paths, so it does not exercise the runtime payload shape.
  WHY: when a consumer wrapper such as `AI Review` fails on a PR, the GitHub workflow_run event delivers a path that ends in `.yml@refs/heads/<branch>`; the literal-path exclusion misses, the triage-workflow-run job condition evaluates true, the reusable workflow is invoked, and a duplicate triage issue for the pipeline wrapper itself is opened instead of being skipped.

The shipped consumer wrappers therefore do not skip and the "skipped wrapper run" guarantee documented in the PR description does not hold at runtime.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml: line 63 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The exclusion list compares unsuffixed paths (e.g., `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`), but `workflow_run.path` at runtime includes a ref suffix (e.g., `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml@refs/heads/main`). GitHub's `contains(array, item)` does exact element matching, so the suffixed runtime path never matches any entry in the unsuffixed exclusion array. `contains` returns `false`, `!contains` returns `true`, and the `triage-workflow-run` job runs for every shipped pipeline workflow failure instead of being excluded.
  WHY: A failed pull-request run of any shipped consumer workflow (AI Review, AI Clarify, AI Implement, etc.) passes the exclusion check and reaches the reusable `check_failure_triage.yml` workflow, opening an unintended `ai:check-triage` issue for a pipeline workflow failure. This is confirmed by `tests/test_review_merge_train.py:719` which uses `"path": ".github/workflows/ai-review.yml@refs/heads/main"` — the ref-suffixed format the merge train already handles (issue #5443). The trigger test at `tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:129` generates unsuffixed paths (`f".github/workflows/{path.name}"`), so it passes but does not cover the runtime path format.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
